s: Where was the 3.1-petaflop supercomputer Param Shakti launched by MeitY?
x: Param Shakti, funded under the National Supercomputing Mission, was launched by MeitY at IIT Madras.

s: In which unit is bandwidth, the data-transfer rate, measured?
x: Bandwidth is measured in bits per second; clock speed is in hertz.

s: What is the full form of MIPS?
x: MIPS = Million Instructions Per Second.

s:
Consider the following statements about Param Shakti:
1. It is a 3.1-petaflop supercomputer.
2. It was launched at IIT Madras.
3. It was built under the Digital India Mission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Param Shakti (3.1 petaflops) was launched by MeitY at IIT Madras under the National Supercomputing Mission.

s: Which Indian supercomputer, built by CRL (Tata), was ranked 4th in the world in November 2007?
x: Eka of CRL (Tata) was ranked 4th in November 2007, when IBM Blue Gene/L was the fastest.

s: Which was the world's fastest supercomputer in 2007, when India's Eka ranked 4th?
x: In 2007 IBM Blue Gene/L was the fastest; India's Eka (CRL, Tata) was 4th in November 2007.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its file type?
x: MP4 stands for MPEG-4 Part 14 and is a video file format. MP3 is audio, PDF is a document format and MOV is a video format.

s: How many bits does ASCII, the character-encoding scheme for 128 characters, use?
x: ASCII is a 7-bit code (2^7 = 128 characters); Unicode extends its range.

s: The communication from a computer mouse to the computer is an example of which transmission mode?
x: A mouse only sends signals to the computer, so the communication is one-way, or simplex (APPSC 2019). Half duplex is two-way but one direction at a time, as in a walkie-talkie. Full duplex is two-way at once, as in a telephone. Multiplexing combines several signals on one channel; it is not a direction mode.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: PNG stands for Portable Network Graphics, not Portable Network Graphics Interface. AVI, MOV and GIF are correctly matched.

s: What is the full form of PDF?
x: PDF is Adobe's Portable Document Format.

s: Which company developed the AVI (Audio Video Interleave) format?
x: AVI is Microsoft's; MOV is Apple's, PDF Adobe's and GIF CompuServe's.

s: A telephone call is an example of which transmission mode?
x: A telephone is full duplex; television is simplex and a walkie-talkie half duplex.

s: For which type of content is MP3 a file format?
x: MP3 (MPEG-1 Audio Layer 3) is an audio format; MP4, MOV and AVI are video formats.

s: What is the full form of JPEG?
x: JPEG = Joint Photographic Experts Group; it is a lossy image format.

s: Which of the following is an example of half-duplex communication?
x: In half duplex, data flows both ways but one at a time, as in a walkie-talkie; television is simplex and telephone full duplex.

s: By which process does an LED produce light?
x: An LED (Light Emitting Diode) gives light by electroluminescence at a semiconductor p-n junction.

s: What is the full form of ASCII?
o: American Standard Code for Information Interchange
American Standard Code for International Interchange
Advanced Standard Code for Information Interchange
American Symbolic Code for Information Interchange
x: ASCII = American Standard Code for Information Interchange; a 7-bit code for 128 characters.

s: Which character-encoding standard extends the 7-bit ASCII code?
x: ASCII is 7-bit with 128 characters; Unicode extends it.

s: ICT is an umbrella term for devices and applications used to do what?
o: replace all forms of human communication
access, store, transmit and manipulate digital information
x: ICT covers devices and applications used to access, store, transmit and manipulate digital information, including mobiles, networks, software, the internet and satellites.

s: Among which of the following does ICT aim to make communication smooth?
x: ICT aims at efficient human-human, human-machine and machine-to-machine communication.

s: Who coined the term 'Cybernetics', the study of automation and communication between human and machine?
x: Cybernetics was named by Norbert Wiener.

s: Which technology makes machines intelligent so that they can mimic human actions?
x: Artificial Intelligence boosts human abilities by making machines intelligent and mimicking human actions.

s: Which of the following is an example of technology preservation?
x: A computer museum preserves old technology, so it is an example of technology preservation.

s: ICT aims at smooth communication between humans, between humans and machines, and between machines. What is the last of these called?
x: Machine-to-machine (M2M) communication is one aim of ICT, along with human-human and human-machine communication.

s: Which of the following is a concern linked with the spread of ICT?
x: Concerns of ICT include privacy risks, the digital divide, job insecurity and over-reliance on technology.

s: In a URL, which part comes immediately after the protocol (such as https://)?
x: A URL has the protocol, then the domain name, then the path to the file.

s: Which of the following indexes webpages so that they can be found?
x: A search engine indexes pages; a web server stores and serves them and a browser displays them.

s: What is the main role of the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C)?
o: Assign MAC addresses to network cards
Operate the global DNS root servers
x: W3C develops and maintains web standards so that webpages function consistently across different browsers.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its description?
o: Surface web — not indexed by search engines
Deep web — entirely associated with illegal markets
Dark web — hidden subset of the deep web requiring tools such as Tor or I2P
Surface web — accessible only through anonymous networks
x: The dark web is a small hidden subset of the deep web and is associated with anonymous access through tools such as Tor or I2P. The surface web is indexed, while the deep web is not necessarily malicious.

s: What is the full form of HTML?
x: Webpages are marked up with HTML, HyperText Markup Language.

s: In which year was the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) founded?
x: Tim Berners-Lee founded W3C in 1994, five years after inventing the WWW.

s: What is the full form of URL?
x: URL = Uniform Resource Locator.

s: About what share of the web is the deep web, not indexed by search engines?
x: The deep web is about 90-95% of the web; the surface web is about 4-5%.

s: What does Web 3.0 refer to?
o: The third generation of the web
x: Web 3.0 is the third generation of the web, changing how it is used and how services are delivered.

s: Which of the following is NOT a web browser?
x: Baidu is a Chinese search engine; Firefox, Opera and Vivaldi are web browsers.

s: Which of the following is needed to access the dark web?
x: The dark web is a hidden part of the deep web reached through Tor or I2P.

s: What is the full form of OCEN?
x: OCEN is the Open Credit Enablement Network, which aims to make lending easy so small borrowers get good credit terms.

s: Which company released Java Server Pages (JSP) in 1999?
x: JSP (Java Server Pages), used to make live web pages, was released in 1999 by Sun Microsystems.

s: In which year was the OSI model ratified?
x: The seven-layer OSI model was ratified in 1984; 1969 is ARPANET, 1989 is WWW and 1994 is W3C.

s: Which network device forwards frames using MAC addresses?
x: A switch forwards frames by MAC address; a hub broadcasts to all ports, a router routes by IP and a modem converts signals.

s: In the OSI model, which layer lies immediately below the Presentation layer?
x: From the top the OSI order is Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link and Physical, so Session lies just below Presentation.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
x: A modem is associated with the Physical layer because it modulates and demodulates signals; it is not a Transport-layer device.

s: Encryption, compression and data formats are functions of which OSI layer?
x: Encryption, compression and formats belong to the Presentation layer; the Transport layer uses TCP and UDP.

s: Which device regenerates a weak signal to extend a network along the cable?
x: A repeater regenerates or amplifies a weak signal; a hub only broadcasts to all ports.

s: Which device joins networks that use different protocols?
x: A gateway joins networks using different protocols.

s: A router works at which layer of the OSI model?
x: A router routes by IP at Layer 3 (Network); a switch works at Layer 2.

s: TCP and UDP belong to which OSI layer?
x: TCP and UDP work at the Transport layer (Layer 4).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the modem?
o: It converts digital to analog and analog to digital
It works at the Transport layer
It links a microcomputer with the telephone line
x: The modem works at the Physical layer, not the Transport layer.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: A switch works at Layer 2 using MAC addresses; a router works at Layer 3 using IP addresses; a hub is a Physical-layer device.

s: How many layers are there in the OSI model?
x: The OSI model has seven layers, from Application at the top to Physical at the bottom.

s: Which is the top layer of the OSI model?
x: The Application layer (HTTP, FTP, SMTP, DNS) is the top layer; the Physical layer is the bottom.

s: ARPANET, established in 1969, was developed under which organisation and is regarded as the forerunner of the Internet?
x: ARPANET was developed under the United States Department of Defense in 1969 and became the forerunner of the Internet.

s: On which date did VSNL launch public internet in India?
x: VSNL launched public internet on 15 August 1995, after ERNET (1986) and before Satyam Infoway became the first private ISP (1998).

s: Which was India's first academic network (1986)?
x: ERNET (1986) was India's academic network; VSNL launched public internet in 1995.

s: Which was India's first private Internet Service Provider (1998)?
x: Satyam Infoway (Sify) became India's first private ISP in 1998.

s: Where did Tim Berners-Lee invent the World Wide Web in 1989?
x: The WWW was invented at CERN in 1989; ARPANET was a US DoD project.

s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. WWW invented
2. ARPANET
3. ERNET
4. VSNL public internet in India
x: ARPANET (1969), ERNET (1986), WWW (1989), VSNL public internet (1995).

s:
Consider the following statements about TCP/IP:
1. TCP makes sure no part of the data goes missing.
2. IP handles addressing and routing.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: TCP gives reliable delivery by checking that nothing is missing; IP addresses and routes the data.

s: Which protocol assigns IP addresses automatically?
x: DHCP assigns IP addresses automatically; DNS turns domain names into IP addresses and TCP ensures reliable delivery.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: POP3 – Downloads mail to one device
IMAP – Deletes mail from the server after downloading it to one device
x: IMAP keeps mail on the server and synchronises it across devices; it is POP3 that usually deletes mail from the server after download.

s: Through which of the following does HTTPS encrypt the traffic between the browser and the server?
x: HTTPS is more secure than HTTP because it encrypts browser-server traffic through TLS.

s: HTTP primarily specifies which of the following?
o: How messages pass between web browsers and web servers
How domain names are converted into IP addresses
How wireless devices communicate within a PAN
How e-mails are downloaded to a device
x: HTTP specifies the communication of messages between web browsers and web servers. DNS, POP3 and Bluetooth serve different functions.

s: Which element of a protocol specifies the format of data?
x: Syntax specifies the format of data, semantics the meaning of each field, and timing when and how fast data is sent.

s: Which protocol is used to send e-mail?
x: SMTP sends e-mail; POP3 and IMAP receive it.

s:
Consider the following statements about e-mail protocols:
1. SMTP sends e-mail.
2. POP3 keeps mail on the server.
3. IMAP keeps mail synced across devices.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: SMTP sends and IMAP keeps mail on the server; POP3 usually deletes mail from the server.

s: Which protocol keeps e-mail on the server, synced across devices?
x: IMAP keeps mail on the server; POP3 downloads and usually deletes it; SMTP sends.

s: What is the full form of DNS?
x: DNS (Domain Name System) turns domain names into IP addresses.

s: Which type of network does a firm linking its LANs in Mumbai, Bengaluru and New Delhi use?
x: Linking LANs in different cities needs a WAN; a MAN covers only a city and a PAN links personal devices (APPSC 2019).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about network topologies?
o: In a bus topology, all nodes share one backbone cable
In a star topology, failure of one node stops the whole network
In a ring topology, each node is linked to two neighbours
A mesh topology links every node to every other node
x: In a star, a failed node is only isolated; it is a hub failure that stops the whole network.

s: Which network topology is the most resilient?
x: In a mesh every node links to every other, making it the most resilient and costliest.

s: A full mesh network of n nodes needs how many links?
x: A mesh needs n(n-1)/2 links.

s: In which topology does the failure of the central hub stop the whole network?
x: In a star, a failed node is only isolated, but hub failure stops all.

s: Which IEEE standard does Ethernet, an example of LAN, follow?
x: Ethernet uses IEEE 802.3; Wi-Fi uses 802.11 and Bluetooth 802.15.1.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
x: A WAN spans large areas and links LANs; personal devices form a PAN.

s: What does a Virtual Private Network mainly provide?
o: A replacement for all network protocols
A wireless connection restricted to one room
A physical cable exclusively owned by a user
An encrypted tunnel over a public network
x: A VPN creates an encrypted tunnel through a public network, improving the privacy of communication.

s: An IPv6 address is how many bits long?
x: IPv6 addresses are 128 bits (eight hexadecimal groups); IPv4 is 32 bits and a MAC address 48 bits.

s: What is the first-octet range of IPv4 Class D (multicast) addresses?
x: Class D is 224–239 for multicast; 240–255 is Class E, 192–223 Class C and 128–191 Class B.

s: An IPv4 address is how many bits long?
x: IPv4 is 32 bits; IPv6 is 128 and a MAC address 48 bits.

s: What is the first-octet range of IPv4 Class C addresses?
For what purpose are IPv4 Class E addresses (240–255) used?
x: Class E is experimental; Class D is multicast.

s: How is an IPv6 address written?
o: 4 groups of decimal separated by dots
6 groups of binary separated by dashes
8 groups of hexadecimal separated by colons
x: IPv6 uses 8 hexadecimal groups separated by colons; IPv4 uses dotted decimal.

s: At which layer of the OSI model is the MAC address, programmed into the network card, used?
x: The 48-bit MAC address is burnt into the NIC and is used at the Data Link layer (Layer 2); IP addresses work at the Network layer.

s: Which of the following addresses is 48 bits long?
x: A MAC address is 48 bits (6 bytes, 12 hex digits); IPv4 is 32 bits and IPv6 is 128 bits.

s: Communication through a walkie-talkie is an example of which transmission mode?
x: Half duplex allows two-way transmission one at a time, as in a walkie-talkie; radio/TV is simplex and a telephone call full duplex.

s: Up to what speed does dial-up, the slowest internet connection, work?
x: Dial-up is the slowest connection, up to 56 Kbps.

s: Which medium does cable internet use?
o: Coaxial lines of cable TV companies
x: Cable internet runs over coaxial lines through a cable modem; DSL uses telephone lines.

s: Which internet connection needs no terrestrial wire?
x: Satellite internet uses space, ground and VSAT user segments, with no terrestrial wire.

s: Which medium do DSL internet connections use?
x: DSL uses telephone copper lines; cable internet uses coaxial TV cable and fibre internet uses light pulses in optical fibre.

s: Which of the following is an example of full duplex transmission?
x: In full duplex, data flows both ways at the same time, as in a telephone call.

s: Radio and television broadcasting are examples of which transmission mode?
x: Simplex is one-way transmission, as in radio and TV broadcasts.

s: Which IEEE standard does Bluetooth, a personal area network (PAN) technology, follow?
x: Bluetooth follows IEEE 802.15.1, while Wi-Fi follows IEEE 802.11.

s: Which IEEE standard does Wi-Fi (wireless LAN) follow?
x: Wi-Fi is IEEE 802.11; Ethernet is 802.3 and Bluetooth 802.15.1.

s: Which IEEE standard does Wi-Fi 7 correspond to?
x: Wi-Fi 7 is IEEE 802.11be and works in the 2.4, 5 and 6 GHz bands.

s: Bluetooth 6.0 (August 2024) added which feature?
x: Bluetooth 6.0 added Channel Sounding.

s: What does Li-Fi use to carry data?
x: Li-Fi carries data on LED light, with better bandwidth and security than Wi-Fi.

s:
Consider the following statements about Bluetooth and Wi-Fi:
1. Both use the 2.4 GHz band.
2. Bluetooth also uses the 5 GHz band.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both use 2.4 GHz, but only Wi-Fi also uses 5 GHz.

s: Which technology links devices with each other without a LAN?
x: Wi-Fi Direct connects devices directly, with no LAN in between.

s: In which year was NIXI, the body under MeitY that runs the .in registry and IRINN, established?
x: NIXI was established in 2003 and runs internet exchange points, the .in registry and IRINN.

s: A website opens for users of one ISP but not for users of another. What is the likely cause?
o: ISP-level DNS poisoning, HTTP interception or SNI filtering
Expiry of the website's domain name
x: ISPs may block sites through DNS poisoning, HTTP interception or SNI filtering, so access differs between ISPs; the other causes would affect all users.

s: Chief Minister Naidu and Sunil Mittal discussed which of the following for Andhra Pradesh?
o: Last-mile connectivity, data centres and an undersea cable landing station
Coal mining, irrigation dams and inland waterways
Satellite launching and missile testing facilities
Steel plants, minor ports and airports
x: The discussion concerned last-mile connectivity, data centres and an undersea cable landing station for Andhra Pradesh.

s: With which of the following is ICANN, set up in 1998 as a United States non-profit, mainly associated?
o: Coordinating the global domain name system and IP address allocation
x: ICANN coordinates the global Domain Name System and IP address allocation. It was established in 1998 as a US non-profit organisation.

s: Who launched BhashaNet (2022), which promotes Universal Acceptance for Indian languages?
x: BhashaNet is a MeitY-NIXI initiative, not ICANN's.

s: Which law did the Telecommunications Act, 2023 replace?
x: The Telecommunications Act, 2023 replaced the Telegraph Act, 1885, and holds the power to suspend internet services.

s: BhashaNet promotes the .Bharat domain in which script?
x: BhashaNet by MeitY-NIXI promotes Universal Acceptance, including .Bharat in Devanagari.

s: Which of the following powers is held under the Telecommunications Act, 2023?
x: The 2023 Act holds the power to suspend internet services; ICANN manages global DNS and NIXI the .in registry.

s: Under which Sections of the IT Act, 2000 can the government order ISPs to block content?
x: Sections 69A and 79 of the IT Act allow blocking orders to ISPs and intermediaries.

s:
Consider the following statements about ICANN and NIXI:
1. ICANN manages the global Domain Name System.
2. NIXI runs the .in registry.
3. BhashaNet is an initiative of ICANN.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: ICANN manages the global DNS and NIXI runs the .in registry; BhashaNet is by MeitY-NIXI, not ICANN.

s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, how many internet connections did India have in 2024?
x: Internet connections rose from 25.15 crore in 2014 to 96.96 crore in 2024.

s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, BharatNet fibre reaches how many gram panchayats?
x: The Economic Survey 2025-26 says BharatNet fibre reaches 2.18 lakh gram panchayats.

s: What does 'Universal Acceptance' mean in internet governance?
o: All browsers display web pages the same way
Every app and e-mail system accepts all domain names and e-mail IDs, including those in Indian scripts
Every citizen gets free internet access
All countries follow one global internet law
x: Universal Acceptance means all domain names and e-mail IDs, including internationalised ones in Indian scripts, work everywhere; BhashaNet promotes it.

s: Which was the first Indian news agency to offer syndicated video news?
x: ANI, established in 1971, was the first Indian news agency to offer syndicated video news.

s: Where are e-journals published?
x: e-journals are electronic journals published on the Internet. Printed paper and microfilm are physical formats, and television broadcasting carries audio-visual programmes, not journals.

s: Which company makes the Final Cut Pro (FCP) video editing software?
x: FCP is Apple's professional non-linear video editor; Premiere Pro is Adobe's.

s: From where does DTH television receive signals?
x: DTH brings signals from geostationary satellites straight to home dishes, bypassing cable operators.

s: When was DD Free Dish, India's first free DTH service, launched?
x: DD Free Dish launched in December 2004 as DD Direct+ and was renamed in 2013.

s:
Consider the following statements about multimedia:
1. Its components include text, graphics, audio, video and animation.
2. A podcast is a radio programme shared via the internet.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Multimedia combines text, graphics, audio, video and animation; a podcast is a radio programme shared via the internet.

s: Which body measures television ratings in India, replacing TAM?
x: The Broadcast Audience Research Council (BARC), set up in 2015, measures TV ratings and replaced TAM.

s:
Match the following:
List-I
A. Innuendo
B. Semiotics
C. Infomercial
D. Technological determinism
List-II
1. Paid programming
2. Study of signs and symbols
3. Technology drives social change
4. Defamation by implication
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Innuendo is defamation by implication, semiotics studies signs, an infomercial is paid programming, and technological determinism (McLuhan) says technology drives social change.

s: What is a Heliodisplay?
o: A mid-air display that projects images onto a thin layer of mist
x: A Heliodisplay projects images onto a thin layer of mist or fog in mid-air, with no physical screen.

s: Who among the following is linked with the idea of technological determinism?
x: Marshall McLuhan is linked with technological determinism, the idea that technology drives social change; Saussure and Peirce are linked with semiotics.

s: From which city is The Wall Street Journal, a business daily, published?
x: The Wall Street Journal is a business daily from New York, USA, owned by Dow Jones (News Corp).

s: In news reporting, what are 'knowledgeable sources'?
o: Sources that are not official but have access to official information
x: 'Knowledgeable sources' are not official sources, but they have access to official information.

s: For what purpose is Adobe Premiere Pro software used?
x: Adobe Premiere Pro, like Apple's Final Cut Pro, is video editing software.

s: Which is the dominant 4G technology that uses OFDM and MIMO?
x: 4G runs on LTE using OFDM and MIMO; WiMAX lost out to LTE.

s: Who made the first handheld mobile phone call on 3 April 1973?
x: Martin Cooper of Motorola made the first handheld mobile call on 3 April 1973. Bell is linked with the telephone, Marconi with radio, and Jack Dorsey co-founded Twitter.

s: Which company designed QR (Quick Response) codes in 1994 for the car industry?
x: Denso Wave designed QR codes in Japan in 1994 for the car industry.

s: Over what range does Near Field Communication (NFC) work?
x: NFC works over only a few centimetres at 106-424 kbps and uses less power than Bluetooth.

s: In which state was Mobile Number Portability first piloted in India?
x: MNP was piloted in Haryana on 25 November 2010 and went pan-India on 20 January 2011.

s: When did pan-India Mobile Number Portability begin?
x: MNP went pan-India on 20 January 2011; full nationwide porting started 3 July 2015.

s: In which year was the QR code designed?
x: Denso Wave designed the QR code in 1994, not 1996.

s: What was India's rank among world telecom markets as of May 2025?
x: India is the world's second-largest telecom market (May 2025).

s: When is 6G mobile technology expected?
x: 6G is expected in the early 2030s; 4G runs on LTE.

s:
Consider the following statements about NFC:
1. Its range is a few centimetres.
2. It uses more power than Bluetooth.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: NFC works over a few centimetres and uses less power than Bluetooth.

s: What is the full form of SIM?
x: SIM is the Subscriber Identity Module, a small card that identifies the subscriber and lets the phone join a mobile network.

s: Which version of Android was released for Pixel phones in June 2025?
x: Android 16 was released for Pixel phones in June 2025.

s: Which of the following payments has RBI allowed over Near Field Communication (NFC)?
x: RBI allowed offline UPI Lite payments using NFC, which works over a few centimetres.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: SMTP — receiving e-mail from a mail server
POP3/IMAP — sending e-mail to a mail server
BCC — displaying all recipients to one another
x: SMTP is used for sending e-mail. POP3 and IMAP are used for receiving mail, while BCC hides recipients from one another.

s: Which e-mail field sends copies to several recipients without revealing their addresses to one another?
x: BCC (blind carbon copy) hides the recipients' addresses from one another.

s: Which one of the following is NOT among the essentials of video conferencing?
x: Video conferencing needs a camera, microphone, speaker/display, a broadband link and conferencing software (codec). An RFID reader is used to read RFID tags and is not a video-conferencing component.

s: What does video conferencing provide?
x: Video conferencing is live two-way video and audio between places.

s: In an e-mail address such as name@gov.in, what does the part after the '@' sign show?
x: An e-mail address has two parts: the user name before '@' and the domain name after it.

s: Which company has owned LinkedIn since 2016?
x: LinkedIn has been owned by Microsoft since 2016; Facebook belongs to Meta.

s: Hashtag (#) was popularised on which social-media platform?
x: The hashtag (#) was popularised on Twitter (APPSC 2019), the micro-blogging platform founded by Jack Dorsey and others in 2006 and renamed X in 2023. Facebook and LinkedIn are networking sites and Amazon is an e-commerce company.

s: In which year was Twitter renamed X?
x: Twitter was renamed X in 2023; LinkedIn was founded in 2003, Facebook in 2004, and LinkedIn came under Microsoft in 2016.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Viral — Content spreading rapidly by sharing
Influencer — Content that spreads rapidly through sharing
Wall — Profile space where posts appear on Facebook
x: An influencer is a user whose following can sway opinions and buying decisions. Content spreading rapidly through sharing is described as viral.

s: What does folksonomy refer to in social media?
x: Folksonomy is user-created tagging or social tagging.

s: What is the full form of SMO?
x: SMO = Social Media Optimisation, raising reach through social platforms.

s: Which is the parent company of Facebook?
x: Facebook (2004, Mark Zuckerberg) belongs to Meta Platforms; LinkedIn belongs to Microsoft.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Reid Hoffman founded LinkedIn (2003); Facebook is Mark Zuckerberg's and Twitter Jack Dorsey's.

s: Which of the following is a comedy video website and not a social networking site?
x: Funny or Die is a comedy video site; Friendster, Flickr and Facebook are social networks.

s: Which of the following was an early social network launched in 2002?
x: Friendster (2002) was an early social network; Kurrently is a social media search engine and Funny or Die a comedy video site.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Platform)
A. Facebook
B. Twitter
C. LinkedIn
List-II (Year founded)
1. 2003
2. 2004
3. 2006
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Facebook was founded in 2004, Twitter in 2006 and LinkedIn in 2003.

s: In which year was Facebook founded by Mark Zuckerberg?
x: Facebook was co-founded by Mark Zuckerberg in 2004; its parent is now Meta Platforms.

s: What type of service is Twitter (now X)?
x: Twitter, founded in 2006 and renamed X in 2023, is a micro-blogging service.

s: On Facebook, what is the profile space where posts appear called?
x: The wall is the profile space on Facebook where posts appear.

s: Which one of the following is an m-governance application that crowdsources reports of inaccessible places?
x: The Sugamya Bharat app crowdsources reports of inaccessible places and belongs to the m-governance sector.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: SWAYAM provides free online courses. Tele-MANAS concerns tele-mental health, Sugamya Bharat concerns accessibility reporting, and UMANG is a governance application.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with its digital-health function?
o: Doctor on Demand — United States health application
x: Agrimarket is an m-agriculture application. eSanjeevani provides telemedicine, Tele-MANAS concerns tele-mental health, and Doctor on Demand is a US health application.

s: For what purpose is the Tele-MANAS mobile health service used?
x: Tele-MANAS provides tele mental health; eSanjeevani provides telemedicine.

s: What is the full form of UMANG?
o: Universal Mobile App for National Governance
Universal Mobile Application for New Growth
Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance
x: UMANG is the Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance, an m-governance app.

s: SWAYAM, which offers free online courses, is an example of which type of mobile application?
x: SWAYAM is an m-learning platform with free online courses.

s: Which mobile app uses GPS to give crop prices at markets within 50 km, using data from Agmarknet?
x: Agrimarket is an m-agriculture app that uses GPS to show crop prices in markets within 50 km, using Agmarknet data.

s: In which year was the Digital India programme launched?
x: Digital India was launched in 2015 and completed 11 years in 2026.

s: What is ONDC?
o: A single e-commerce platform owned by one seller
A payment gateway regulated by RBI
x: ONDC is a network-based protocol, not a single platform; it connects buyer and seller apps across B2C and B2B and aims to help MSMEs.

s: Which of the following pairs (e-commerce model – transaction) is correctly matched?
o: B2C – Consumer sells to another consumer
C2C – Business sells to another business
D2C – Brand sells directly to the consumer without a middleman
B2B – Business sells to the consumer
x: D2C is direct brand-to-consumer selling; B2B is business-to-business, B2C business-to-consumer and C2C consumer-to-consumer.

s: In which model of e-commerce is 100% FDI under the automatic route permitted?
x: 100% FDI under the automatic route is allowed in the marketplace model, while FDI is not permitted in the inventory model.

s: OLX-type resale is an example of which e-commerce model?
x: OLX-type resale is consumer to consumer (C2C).

s: IndiaMART is an example of which e-commerce model?
x: IndiaMART is business to business (B2B).

s:
Consider the following statements about ONDC:
1. It is an open, network-based protocol.
2. It is a payment gateway.
3. It connects buyer apps to seller apps across B2C and B2B.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: ONDC is an open protocol linking buyer and seller apps across B2C and B2B; it is not a payment gateway or a single platform.

s:
Consider the following statements about FDI in e-commerce:
1. 100% FDI is allowed under the automatic route in the marketplace model.
2. 100% FDI is allowed in the inventory model.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 100% FDI under the automatic route is allowed in the marketplace model; no FDI is allowed in the inventory model.

s: In the D2C e-commerce model:
o: A brand sells directly to consumers
x: D2C means the brand sells directly to the consumer without a middleman.

s: In which city was ONDC (Open Network for Digital Commerce) beta-tested?
x: ONDC, an open network-based protocol for e-commerce, was beta-tested in Bengaluru.

s: Under the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025, the Online Gaming Authority of India is a digital attached office of which ministry?
o: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
x: OGAI is a digital attached office of MeitY, not the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting; the Act also banned real-money gaming.

s: In which law were gig and platform workers defined for the first time?
o: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
x: The Code on Social Security, 2020 first defined gig and platform workers; aggregators contribute to their social-security fund.

s: Under which Act are the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 framed?
x: The Rules are under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and cover both marketplace and inventory entities.

s: The IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 were framed under which section of the IT Act?
x: The Rules were framed under Section 87; Section 79 is the safe-harbour provision.

s:
Consider the following statements about the IT Amendment Rules, 2023:
1. An intermediary ignoring government orders on false content may lose safe-harbour protection.
2. Safe-harbour protection is provided under Section 87 of the IT Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: An intermediary ignoring such orders may lose safe harbour, but safe harbour is under Section 79, not Section 87.

s: What does the proposed separate law on age-based access to social media favour?
o: A ban limited only to digital news platforms
A blanket ban for every person below 18 years
Graded limits based on age rather than a blanket ban
x: The proposed approach favours graded limits based on age instead of imposing a blanket ban on all persons below a specified age.

s: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, a 'child' is anyone below what age?
x: The DPDP Act treats anyone below 18 as a child, and Section 9 requires verifiable parental consent for a child's data.

s: From which date did the rules under the Online Gaming Act, 2025 take effect?
x: Rules were notified in April 2026 and took effect from 1 May 2026.

s: What did the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025 ban?
x: The Act banned real-money gaming and created the Online Gaming Authority of India.

s: Which Section of the DPDP Act provides for verifiable parental consent for children?
x: Section 9 of the DPDP Act requires verifiable parental consent; a child is anyone below 18.

s: The IT Rules, 2021 provide a grievance redressal mechanism of how many tiers?
x: The IT Rules 2021 set a Code of Ethics and three-tier grievance redressal.

s: What do the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 require e-commerce entities to display?
x: The rules require a grievance officer and display of country of origin.

s: From which date did the Code on Social Security, along with all four labour codes, come into force?
x: All four labour codes, including the Code on Social Security, are in force from 21 November 2025.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the IT Rules, 2021?
o: They were framed under Section 87 of the IT Act
They regulate social media, OTT and digital news
They were framed under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019
x: The IT Rules 2021 were framed under Section 87 of the IT Act; the E-Commerce Rules 2020 come under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

s: What is endless scrolling through bad news called?
x: Doomscrolling is endless scrolling through bad news; health anxiety from symptom searches is cyberchondria.

s: Which body includes Gaming Disorder in ICD-11?
x: The World Health Organization lists Gaming Disorder in ICD-11.

s: What is the fear of being without one's mobile phone called?
x: Nomophobia is 'no-mobile-phobia'; FOMO is fear of missing out.

s: What is health worry fed by online symptom searches called?
x: Cyberchondria is health anxiety from online symptom searches.

s: What is a deliberate break from digital devices called?
x: A digital detox is a deliberate break from devices.

s: The PRAGYATA framework concerning screen time is a measure of which ministry?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Women and Child Development
x: PRAGYATA is the Ministry of Education's framework, one of the central measures on screen time and digital addiction.

s: 'Digital Detox Centre – Beyond Screens' is an initiative of which state?
x: 'Digital Detox Centre – Beyond Screens' is Karnataka's; Kerala Police run D-DAD centres.

s: The police of which state run D-DAD (Digital De-Addiction) centres?
x: Kerala Police run D-DAD centres; 'Beyond Screens' is Karnataka's.

s: Andhra Pradesh's social-media ban applies to children under what age?
x: AP's ban is for children under 13; Karnataka's is for under 16.

s: Which institution runs the SHUT Clinic for technology addiction?
x: NIMHANS runs the SHUT Clinic.

s: Which was the first Indian state to announce a social-media ban for children under 16?
x: Karnataka was the first state to announce an under-16 ban; AP's ban is for under 13.

s: Which country brought the world's first nationwide under-16 social-media ban (December 2025)?
x: Australia's under-16 ban took effect on 10 December 2025.

s: Which field combines mechanical engineering, electronics and computing?
x: Mechatronics combines mechanical engineering, electronics and computing or robotics.

s: Who developed the humanoid robot Manav?
x: Manav was developed by A-SET Training & Research Institutes, Delhi, not Genrobotics.

s: For which of the following does ISO 10218 set safety norms?
x: ISO 10218 covers industrial-robot safety, not surgical robots; ISO TC 299 is the robotics committee.

s: Which robot was developed to clean manholes and sewers to end manual scavenging?
x: Bandicoot (Genrobotics, Kerala) cleans manholes and sewers; HomoSEP cleans septic tanks, Daksh defuses IEDs and Vyommitra is ISRO's half-humanoid.

s: Which is India's first indigenous surgical robotic system?
x: SSI Mantra, developed by SS Innovations (Dr Sudhir Srivastava), is India's first indigenous surgical robotic system. Manav is India's first 3D-printed humanoid (built in late 2014), not a surgical robot.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the type of robot?
o: Surgical robot — robotic surgery and rehabilitation
x: Surgical or medical robots are used in robotic surgery and rehabilitation. Industrial robots are associated with assembly, welding and painting, while service robots serve functions such as hospitality and reception.

s: Who developed HomoSEP, a robot that cleans septic tanks?
x: HomoSEP is from IIT Madras; Bandicoot, which cleans sewers, is from Genrobotics.

s: For what purpose is Vyommitra, a half-humanoid robot developed by ISRO, meant?
x: Vyommitra is ISRO's half-humanoid astronaut for the uncrewed Gaganyaan flight.

s: Which of the following pairs (robot – purpose) is correctly matched?
x: Daksh is DRDO's robot for defusing IEDs; Bandicoot cleans sewers, HomoSEP septic tanks and Vyommitra is for Gaganyaan.

s: A robot used in hospitality, retail or reception belongs to which type?
x: Service robots work in hospitality, retail and reception; industrial robots do assembly, welding and painting.

s: Who developed Bandicoot, the robot that cleans manholes and sewers?
x: Bandicoot was developed by Genrobotics of Kerala to clean manholes and sewers and end manual scavenging.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Bandicoot was developed by Genrobotics, Kerala.
2. HomoSEP was developed by IIT Madras to clean septic tanks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: Bandicoot (Genrobotics) cleans sewers and HomoSEP (IIT Madras) cleans septic tanks.

s: Which organisation developed Daksh, the remotely operated robot used to defuse IEDs?
x: Daksh is a DRDO robot that handles and defuses IEDs.

s: Who developed SSI Mantra, India's first indigenous surgical robotic system?
x: SSI Mantra was developed by SS Innovations, founded by Dr Sudhir Srivastava.

s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh was offered for aerospace, drone and semiconductor manufacturing?
x: Sri Sathya Sai district, near Bengaluru, was offered for aerospace, drone and semiconductor manufacturing.

s: Which of the following pairs (processor – developer) is correctly matched?
x: AJIT was developed by IIT Bombay; DHRUV64 by C-DAC, SHAKTI by IIT Madras and Vikram 3201 by ISRO's Semi-Conductor Laboratory, Chandigarh.

s: In which year was the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) launched?
x: The ISM was launched in 2021 with a ₹76,000 crore PLI outlay.

s: Under Semicon 2.0, up to what share of capital subsidy is given for CMOS silicon fabs?
x: CMOS silicon fabs get up to 40%; compound and display fabs get 35%, R&D up to 75% and conventional packaging 25%.

s: Who developed Vikram 3201, a 32-bit space-grade processor?
x: Vikram 3201 is from ISRO's SCL, Chandigarh; DHRUV64 is C-DAC's 64-bit processor.

s: Which is the only true wafer fab among India's approved semiconductor units?
x: Tata-PSMC Dholera is the wafer fab; Micron and Tata Jagiroad are ATMP units and Kaynes is OSAT.

s: Which of the following pairs (semiconductor unit – state) is correctly matched?
x: Tata's Jagiroad (Morigaon) ATMP unit is in Assam; Micron Sanand and Tata-PSMC Dholera are in Gujarat.

s: With what outlay was Semicon 2.0 (ISM Phase 2) notified?
x: Semicon 2.0 carries ₹1,27,500 crore; ₹76,000 crore was the original ISM outlay.

s: Which organisation developed the 64-bit RISC-V processor DHRUV64?
x: DHRUV64 is a 64-bit RISC-V processor of C-DAC; SHAKTI is from IIT Madras and AJIT from IIT Bombay.

s: Which material is used to make computer chips?
x: Integrated circuit chips are made from silicon, a semiconductor.

s: Which device lets current flow in one direction only and converts AC to DC?
x: A diode allows current in one direction only, so it is used for rectification (AC to DC).

s: What is the PLI outlay of the India Semiconductor Mission launched in 2021?
x: The India Semiconductor Mission (2021) has a ₹76,000 crore PLI outlay; ₹1,27,500 crore is Semicon 2.0.

s: Which institution developed the SHAKTI processor?
x: SHAKTI is a RISC-V processor developed by IIT Madras.

s: Which technology creates a fully computer-generated world that shuts out the real world?
x: A fully computer-generated world is VR; AR places digital layers over the real world and XR is an umbrella term for VR, AR and MR.

s: Where is the VR/AR Centre of Excellence (VARCoE), set up by MeitY and STPI with Odisha, located?
x: VARCoE is at IIT Bhubaneswar with Odisha as partner; the IMAGE CoE, partnered by Telangana, is at Hyderabad.

s: With reference to Virtual Reality (VR), which one of the following is correct?
o: It overlays digital layers on the real world, as in Pokemon Go.
It creates a fully computer-generated, immersive world in which the user is still a real person.
It replaces the user with a computer-generated avatar who is not a real person.
It is the umbrella term covering AR and MR.
x: VR is a fully computer-generated, immersive world; the person experiencing it is still a real person (APPSC 2024). Overlaying digital layers on the real world is AR, and the umbrella term for VR, AR and MR is XR.

s: In which technology do real and virtual objects interact in real time?
x: In Mixed Reality real and virtual objects interact in real time; AR only lays digital layers over the real world.

s:
Consider the following statements about extended reality:
1. Augmented Reality blocks out the physical world.
2. In Virtual Reality, the user is still a real person.
3. Extended Reality is an umbrella term for VR, AR and MR.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: AR places digital layers over the real world without blocking it, so 1 is wrong; 2 and 3 are correct.

s: Where is the IMAGE Centre of Excellence for gaming, VFX, computer vision and AI, set up by MeitY, STPI and Telangana, located?
x: IMAGE CoE is in Hyderabad; VARCoE is at IIT Bhubaneswar.

s: What is a persistent, shared 3D virtual space using XR, avatars and digital assets called?
x: The metaverse is a persistent, shared 3D virtual space built on XR, avatars and digital assets.

s: Who coined the term 'augmented reality' in 1990?
x: Thomas Caudell of Boeing coined 'augmented reality' in 1990.

s: What is printing that adds materials which change shape over time called?
x: 4D printing adds materials that change shape over time; additive manufacturing (3D printing) builds layer by layer from a CAD model.

s: By what other name is 3D printing known?
x: 3D printing is additive manufacturing, building objects layer by layer from a CAD model; it is not subtractive.

s: Where and when was India's first 3D-printed post office set up?
x: India’s first 3D-printed post office was established in Bengaluru in 2023.

s: Which of the following is NOT an application of 3D printing?
x: 3D printing is used in food, health (bionic ears), automotive, aerospace and construction; converting AC to DC is done by a diode.

s: In how many days was India's first 3D-printed post office in Bengaluru built?
x: India's first 3D-printed post office (Bengaluru, 2023, 1,021 sq ft) was built in 43 days.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding IoT and AI?
o: IoT devices collect and exchange data through sensors
A smart thermostat is an example of AI rather than IoT
AI analyses data, recognises patterns and makes decisions
Chatbots and image recognition are examples of AI
x: A smart thermostat is listed as an IoT example, not an AI example.

s: What does the Internet of Things (IoT) refer to?
o: A network limited to industrial robots
Only computers connected through wired networks
A system in which data can be exchanged only after manual approval
Devices with sensors linked in a network and exchanging data without human intervention
x: IoT consists of sensor-equipped devices connected through networks that exchange data without human intervention.

s: Which policy covers 5G, the Internet of Things (IoT) and machine-to-machine (M2M) communication?
x: The National Digital Communications Policy (NDCP) 2018 covers 5G, IoT and M2M. The Drone Rules 2021 govern drones, the IT Rules 2021 regulate intermediaries and digital media, and the E-Commerce Rules 2020 protect online consumers.

s: Which of the following correctly represents the three-layer model of the Internet of Things, from the device-facing layer to the user-facing layer?
x: The three-layer IoT model consists of the perception layer, network layer and application layer. The perception layer senses, the network layer transmits and the application layer provides smart services.

s: Where are the IoT Centres of Excellence set up through the MeitY-NASSCOM initiative located?
x: The MeitY-NASSCOM IoT Centres of Excellence are located at Bengaluru, Gurugram, Gandhinagar and Visakhapatnam.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Internet of Mobile Things — mass production assembly lines
x: Internet of Mobile Things concerns mobile devices or mobile objects. Industrial automation is associated with IIoT, nano-devices with IoNT and military applications with mission-critical IoT.

s: Which IoT variant is concerned with nano-devices?
x: IoNT is the Internet of Nano Things; IIoT is industrial automation and mission-critical IoT is military.

s: The four-stage model of IoT adds which layer to the perception, network and application layers?
x: The four-stage version is perception, transport, network and application.

s: Smart farming, smart homes and smart grids are applications of which technology?
x: IoT applications include smart farming, smart homes, smart grids, healthcare, logistics and smart cities.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Internet of Things:
1. A smart thermostat is an example of IoT rather than AI.
2. IIoT is concerned with industrial automation.
3. The Internet of Mobile Things is concerned with assembly lines.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: A smart thermostat is IoT and IIoT is industrial; the Internet of Mobile Things concerns mobile objects, not assembly lines.

s: Who coined the term 'Internet of Things' in 1999?
x: Kevin Ashton coined 'Internet of Things' in 1999; Klaus Schwab popularised 'Fourth Industrial Revolution'.

s: Tracking heart rate, steps and sleep is a typical function of which of the following?
x: Wearables such as smartwatches and fitness bands track health indicators and act as IoT end-devices.

s: A semi-passive RFID tag differs from an active RFID tag because the semi-passive tag:
o: Uses its battery to run the chip but uses the reader’s field to reply
Has no internal power and cannot contain identity data
Has an independent transmitter and broadcasts over a long range
Uses only a satellite signal for communication
x: A semi-passive tag’s battery powers its chip, but it still uses the reader’s field to send its response. An active tag has its own battery and transmitter.

s: What is an RFID tag that has its own battery and transmitter called?
x: An active tag has its own battery and transmitter; a passive tag has no battery and backscatters the reader's signal.

s: How does a passive RFID tag reply to the reader?
o: Using a battery that runs a transmitter
Using a battery that runs the chip only
x: Passive tags have no battery and backscatter the reader's signal; active tags broadcast with their own transmitter.

s: What are drone swarms?
o: Large drones operated manually by a single pilot from different locations
Many drones coordinated by software for surveillance, light shows or strikes
Drones restricted exclusively to agricultural spraying
Fixed-wing aircraft that cannot exchange operational data
x: A drone swarm consists of many drones coordinated through software and may be used for surveillance, light shows or strikes.

s: Kisan drones are primarily associated with which of the following activities?
o: Operating light shows and conducting strikes
x: Kisan drones are used to spray crops and map land; 100 were flagged off in February 2022.

s: To whom does the Namo Drone Didi initiative provide drones?
o: women’s Self-Help Groups for agricultural services
DGCA training institutes for flight certification
x: Namo Drone Didi provides drones to women’s Self-Help Groups for agricultural services.

s: Which of the following is NOT a measure identified for making India a global drone hub by 2030?
o: A ban on DGCA-approved training institutes
Production Linked Incentive for drones and components
x: The measures include liberalised Drone Rules, 2021, DigitalSky, PLI, Drone Shakti, DGCA-approved training institutes and Bharat Drone Mahotsav. A ban on such institutes is contrary to the stated approach.

s: Under the Drone Rules, 2021, in which class is a drone weighing 25-150 kg placed?
x: 25-150 kg is the medium class; small is 2-25 kg and large is above 150 kg.

s: Where is the AP Drone City coming up?
x: AP Drone City is at Orvakal, Kurnool, on 300 acres; its foundation was laid on 14 Nov 2025.

s: What is the outlay of the PLI scheme for drones (2021)?
x: PLI for drones gives ₹120 crore over three years from 2021-22; ₹1,261 crore is Namo Drone Didi.

s: Which is India's online permission platform for drones?
x: DigitalSky is the permission platform under the liberalised Drone Rules 2021.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Namo Drone Didi scheme?
o: It provides drones to women SHGs for agri-services
It has an outlay of ₹1,261 crore
x: Namo Drone Didi covers 15,000 SHGs, not 1,500.

s: How many Kisan drones were flagged off in February 2022?
x: 100 Kisan drones, used for spraying crops and mapping land, were flagged off in February 2022.

s: Under the Drone Rules, 2021, up to what weight is a drone classed as a nano drone?
x: Nano drones weigh up to 250 g; micro drones are 250 g to 2 kg.

s: Under the Drone Rules, 2021, in which class are drones weighing more than 150 kg placed?
x: Drones above 150 kg are large; 25-150 kg is medium and 2-25 kg is small.

s: What was the defining technology of Industry 3.0?
x: Industry 1.0 used steam, 2.0 electricity and mass production, 3.0 computers and electronics, and 4.0 cyber-physical systems.

s: Steam-powered weaving looms are a feature of which stage of the industrial revolution?
x: Steam-powered looms belong to Industry 1.0, while Industry 4.0 is marked by cyber-physical systems, IoT, AI and big data.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Fourth Industrial Revolution:
1. The term was coined by Klaus Schwab, founder of the World Economic Forum, in 2016.
2. It involves the convergence of digital, physical and biological technologies.
3. It is the stage that puts people at the centre of industrial innovation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Schwab coined the term in 2016 and it merges digital, physical and biological technologies; putting people at the centre is the idea of Industry 5.0.

s: SAMARTH Udyog Bharat 4.0, which spreads Industry 4.0 through demonstration centres, is an initiative of which of the following?
x: SAMARTH (Smart Advanced Manufacturing and Rapid Transformation Hub) Udyog Bharat 4.0 is a Ministry of Heavy Industries initiative.

s: The World Economic Forum’s proposed Fourth Industrial Revolution Centre in Andhra Pradesh would be India’s:
o: first such centre after Mumbai and Telangana
fourth such centre after Bengaluru, Mumbai and Telangana
third such centre after Mumbai and Telangana
x: The proposed centre in Andhra Pradesh would be India’s third, after the centres in Mumbai and Telangana.

s: What is the main criticism of automation and artificial intelligence?
o: They replace only manual work and have no effect on intellectual work.
They eliminate the need for all forms of industrial training.
They replace intellectual as well as manual work, raising the issue of job displacement.
They are confined to semiconductor fabrication and do not affect employment.
x: The criticism is that automation and AI can replace both intellectual and manual work, thereby raising concerns about job displacement.

s: The term 'Industry 4.0' was coined in which country?
x: 'Industry 4.0' was coined in Germany at the Hannover Fair in 2011.

s: Which of the following is the main feature of Industry 5.0?
x: Industry 5.0 means human-machine collaboration with people at the centre; cyber-physical systems define Industry 4.0.

s: Electricity, mass production and the assembly line were the defining features of which stage of the industrial revolution?
x: Industry 2.0 brought electricity and mass production; Industry 1.0 was steam power and 3.0 automation and computers.

s: How many Technology Innovation Hubs are there under the National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems (NM-ICPS)?
x: NM-ICPS has 25 Technology Innovation Hubs, robotics being one vertical.

s: What is a system in which computing is tightly joined with physical processes, a core element of Industry 4.0, called?
x: A cyber-physical system integrates computing closely with physical processes and is central to Industry 4.0 and NM-ICPS.

s: What is a collaborative robot designed to work safely beside humans called?
x: A cobot is a collaborative robot working alongside humans; remote monitoring of plants and grids is SCADA.

s: In 5G, what is the mMTC (massive machine-type communication) slice meant for?
x: mMTC supports dense IoT sensor deployments in 5G networks.

s: What is a virtual replica of a physical object or system used for simulation and monitoring called?
x: A digital twin is a virtual replica of a physical object or system.

s: In industrial automation, what is the full form of PLC?
x: A Programmable Logic Controller is a rugged industrial computer that controls machines.

s: What is the full form of SCADA, used for remote monitoring of plants and grids?
x: SCADA is Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition, used to monitor plants and grids remotely.
